newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan stocks rise, lifted by blue chips.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan stocks rise, lifted by blue chips.

text.p: The Casablanca stock exchange closed its two-hour session on Monday 0.27 percent higher, lifted mainly by blue chips including Wafabank, a bourse official said.
The all-share index closed at 439.02 points from 437.86 points on Friday.
"The bourse pursues its upward trend due mainly to active trading in the blue-chip firms such as Wafabank and ONA Group," one trader said.

Wafabank has purchased Spanish Uniban bank last week but the final agreement would be sealed when Uniban's general assembly meets on December 30 and after approval by the monetary authorities, officials said.
Wafabank, a very liquid stock, jumped nine dirhams to close at 560 from 551 a week earlier.
Uniban rose two dirhams to close at 114 dirhams, brokers said.
Credit firm Credor which was recently introduced on the stock market, closed at 447 dirhams, up from 434 on Friday.
ONA Group, Morocco's largest private conglomerate, remained unchanged at 500 dirhams.
Traded volume on the official market was 30.1 million dirhams against 19.6 million over the previous session.
